prize_parts.citation: For structural and biochemical discoveries on nitrogenase, establishing the architecture of the MoFe protein and its iron-molybdenum cofactor and the ATP-dependent electron-transfer cycle that drives biological nitrogen fixation

statement.case_for: My preferred position is unchanged: nitrogenase, B009, worded around what has been established. The structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor (Rees), the carbide and ligand-bound states, and recent turnover-state cryo-EM have been reproduced by several groups over about three decades. Seefeldt's kinetics and spectroscopy defined the ATP-coupled electron-transfer cycle, and Dean's genetics and cofactor-biosynthesis work made the protein and its mutants tractable. This is a physically grounded account of electron transfer and substrate binding at an unusual metal cluster, with direct bearing on the nitrogen cycle and ammonia synthesis. In a field this old the achievement is separable and the evidence is not in dispute, which none of the more recent candidates can claim.
statement.case_against: The chemical mechanism of N2 reduction at the cofactor is still unresolved, so the citation must stop at structure, cofactor chemistry and the electron-transfer cycle and must not claim the full catalytic mechanism. Credit is crowded among Rees, Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe, and any three names omit someone with a serious claim. B009 also has two first-choice supporters out of eight, whereas B068 is named in the first choice or alternatives by seven members, and I cannot dismiss that breadth. I again note that my preference is partly shaped by my own interest in biological energy conversion.

responses.point: Zou backs B009 but with Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, and the chair asked whether a structure-and-cofactor citation suffices and whether the third name is Dean or Einsle.
responses.response: I think a structure-and-cofactor citation does suffice, and I have narrowed my wording accordingly. On the third name we still differ. Einsle's atomic-resolution work and the carbide assignment are decisive for cofactor composition, but they build directly on Rees's structures and are shared with him. Dean's contribution is distinct and enabled the rest: the genetics and biochemistry that produced the protein, the cofactor-biosynthesis pathway and the mutants. The carbide result is a single decisive finding. Dean's contribution is a foundation. I would accept Einsle in place of Dean if the expert reports show that the carbide and ligand-bound-state advances were substantially his alone, and I would then regard B009 as equally defensible.

responses.point: Aili holds B068 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, as a designable, catalytic, event-driven chemical principle, while conceding that no PROTAC is approved and that the glue lineage has separate credit.
responses.response: I take the point that degraders are a genuinely new design principle, and B068 is my first alternative. Two things keep it below nitrogenase for me. First, the chair's question, one prize or two, has no clean answer. Chabes states that a PROTAC-only trio leaves out the part of the field with the most patient benefit. A prize that has to ignore the cereblon lineage to fit three names is not attributable as cleanly as you suggest. Second, the mechanistic claims are established for the ternary-complex concept, but the evidence of benefit to patients is still prospective. If the committee judges that one PROTAC-focused citation is fair and the Ciulli name is right, I would not stand in the way, but I do not see it as more mature than B009.

responses.point: Chabes also backs B068 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli but says Handa or Sakamoto could be the third name and that the glue lineage carries the stronger link to approved drugs.
responses.response: Your own reservation is the one I weigh most. If the glue lineage has the stronger clinical record and a distinct origin, then a PROTAC trio would credit the part of the field with less proven benefit and leave out the part with more. That is a scientific and attribution problem and not a matter of wording. I cannot resolve it from the nomination record. It is the main reason I would keep B068 as an alternative and not make it my preferred prize. If it were made one prize, I would expect the citation to say 'chemically induced proximity to E3 ligases' broadly enough to cover both, and I would want the expert report to confirm that the three names then chosen represent both lineages.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, supports B003 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, and asks whether the physical-chemical principle of demixing and multivalency can be cited without asserting in vivo phase separation of specific condensates.
responses.response: A citation limited to demixing and multivalency as a physical principle can be written, and the 2009 droplet observation and Rosen's reconstitution make a defensible origin. My difficulty is that such a citation would be narrower than what the field's impact claims rest on, which is that condensates organize cells. That wider claim is the contested one. I would prefer a prize whose citation the evidence supports without a qualifier, which is why I still place nitrogenase ahead. B003 remains an alternative for me, and I would find Rosen preferable to Pappu or Mittag only if the expert reports show multivalent reconstitution preceding the sequence-grammar work.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports support Einsle ahead of Dean, or Dean ahead of Einsle, for the third place.
Whether a citation limited to structure, cofactor chemistry and the electron-transfer cycle is acceptable to colleagues when the N2 reduction mechanism is unresolved.
Whether Ribbe's claim on cofactor chemistry should displace Dean, which I cannot settle from my recalled literature.
Whether the committee can write B068 as one prize without excluding the glue lineage's clinical record.
I rely on recalled literature and have not verified priority details independently.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged. I work on proton transfer in cytochrome c oxidase, a different enzyme from nitrogenase, and my profile shows no collaboration with any B009 candidate. My interest in biological energy conversion may shade my judgement and I disclose it. Xiaodong Zou is my Stockholm University colleague, but this is not a tie to any shortlisted candidate. I have no conflict with the B068 or B003 candidates.
